Exercising the forecasting workflow

Source: vignettes/zero-shot-workflow.Rmd
zero-shot-workflow.Rmd

This vignette exercises the engine and adapter surfaces with stub, a weight-free random-walk fixture. It is not a foundation model — it exists so the engine and its adapters can be demonstrated and tested without a download.

For the same workflow driven by a real checkpoint, see vignette("timesfm-zero-shot").

Load a model

tsfm_pretrained() returns a uniform model handle. The stub branch is entirely local and deterministic:

library(tsfm)

model <- tsfm_pretrained("stub")

Before doing any work, ask what the model can do. The capability report is checked before inference, so an unsupported request fails fast with a clear message instead of deep inside a tensor op:

tsfm_capabilities(model)
#> <tsfm_capabilities>
#>   architecture:      stub
#>   max_context:       512         quantiles: native
#>   multivariate:      FALSE       samples:   FALSE
#>   past_covariates:   FALSE       future_covariates: FALSE
#>   static_covariates: FALSE       fine_tunable: FALSE
#>   license:           MIT

Path 1 — the forecast() convenience surface (tsibble)

Hand a panel of history and a horizon; get a forecast object back that converts to a fable for the tidyverts accuracy/reconciliation stack:

library(tsibble)

fc <- forecast(model, tourism_history, h = 12,
               quantile_levels = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))

fc |>
  fabletools::as_fable() |>
  fabletools::accuracy(tourism_actuals)

tsfm registers a method on fabletools::as_fable() rather than exporting a generic of its own, so the verb keeps working when fabletools and tsfm are both attached. Call it qualified, or library(fabletools) first.

Path 2 — a tidymodels workflow

The tidymodels surface is a parsnip spec inside a workflow(). The model is chosen by the engine’s model_id; everything else stays the same.

library(parsnip)
library(workflows)

spec <- tsfm_reg(context_length = 512L) |>
  set_engine("tsfm",
             model_id = "stub",
             index    = "date",
             id       = "store")

wf <- workflow() |>
  add_formula(demand ~ date) |>
  add_model(spec)

fit <- fit(wf, data = train_df)
predict(fit, new_data = future_df)   # tibble: .pred

Tuning the context length

context_length is a tunable dials parameter, so a rolling-origin search over rsample resamples works out of the box:

library(tune)
library(rsample)

spec <- tsfm_reg(context_length = tune()) |>
  set_engine("tsfm", model_id = "stub", index = "date", id = "store")

tune_grid(
  workflow() |> add_formula(demand ~ date) |> add_model(spec),
  resamples = sliding_period(train_df, date, "month"),
  grid      = 5
)

Status

The public workflow above is real, but its model is deliberately only a test fixture. TimesFM 2.5 is the first implemented release model. Toto 2.0 4M and a new native Chronos-2 port are required before 0.1.0; the old Chronos-2 Brulee bridge remains unregistered reference work only. TTM is not a current target because the selected small-model slot is probabilistic Toto rather than a point-only checkpoint.
